key_insight: YC-Bench exposes whether LLM-driven agents can sustain coherent strategies over long horizons by simulating a year-long startup run with hundreds of decision points, revealing failures in planning, adaptation, and error compounding that short-horizon tests miss.
problem_solved: Evaluates and quantifies an agent's ability to plan under uncertainty, learn from delayed feedback, and maintain consistent execution when early mistakes compound over many steps.
method: Design a simulated startup environment that runs for a one-year horizon across hundreds of turns, requiring hiring, contracting, task allocation, and financial management.
Run standardized agent configurations through the environment and measure long-term outcomes (profitability, task completion, employee retention) and stability of strategy over time.
Provide diagnostic metrics and scenarios to isolate planning, adaptation, and error-compounding behaviors (e.g., delayed-reward trials, stochastic events, contract variability).
impact: Offers a practical, reproducible benchmark for researchers and engineers to stress-test and improve agents' long-horizon planning and robustness, guiding model design, training regimes, and evaluation standards for real-world sequential decision tasks.
visual_elements: One-year timeline diagram showing hundreds of turns with annotated events (hires, contracts, revenue spikes, failures).
Agent decision loop flowchart: perception → plan → act → delayed feedback → update, highlighting delayed rewards and compounding errors.
KPI dashboard mockup: profit curve, task completion rate, employee churn, and stability score over time.
Heatmap or bar chart comparing agent variants on long-horizon metrics (robustness, adaptability, cumulative reward).
paper_title: $\texttt{YC-Bench}$: Benchmarking AI Agents for Long-Term Planning and Consistent Execution
paper_authors: Muyu He, Adit Jain, Anand Kumar, Vincent Tu, Soumyadeep Bakshi
